title: throughput-driven-staffing-price-buckets-prototype-2027
summary: Prototype spreadsheet tying GPU throughput and token/sec capacity to a pragmatic headcount ladder and a set of price bucket triggers. Purpose: give product + sales a lightweight operational rulebook for when to hire (or pause hires) and when to move customers between price bands based on observed throughput and utilization.
sheet_data:
ASSUMPTIONS:
- Time horizon: 12 months (Nov 2026 - Oct 2027)
- Base model: mix of open large models and optimized quantized variants.
- Unit: revenue measured per 1,000 tokens (1k-tokens).
- Avg tokens per request: 1,200 tokens (weighted by chat+generation).
- GPU node nominal throughput: 30M tokens/day (single A100-like equivalent after batching/kv-cache).
- Ops ratio: 1 SRE per 12 GPU nodes (includes infra automation improvements in H1).
- MLE/Serving engineers scale by model variants: 1 MLE per 8 model-variants actively served.
- Sales/CS quota: 1 AE supports $1.5M ARR on hosted API for target coverage.
- Avg hosted gross margin baseline: 58% at price $0.003 / 1k tokens.

SCENARIO TABLE (monthly snapshot example):
Columns: Scenario | Price per 1k | Daily tokens (M) | Avg utilization (%) | GPUs needed | SREs | Serving Eng | MLEs | AEs | Monthly rev ($k) | Monthly gross ($k)
Base    | $0.0030  | 900              | 55%                | 18         | 2     | 3           | 2    | 2   | 3,240           | 1,879
Growth  | $0.0027  | 1,400            | 70%                | 28         | 3     | 4           | 3    | 3   | 3,402           | 1,973
Conserve| $0.0036  | 600              | 40%                | 12         | 1     | 2           | 1    | 1   | 648             | 374
Notes: 
- GPUs needed = ceil(daily_tokens / (node_throughput * utilization_adjustment)), where node_throughput = 30M tokens/day and utilization_adjustment accounts for scheduling (~0.9).
- Monthly_rev = daily_tokens * 30 * (price_per_1k / 1000)

HEADCOUNT LADDER (rules & thresholds):
- If GPUs <= 12: SREs = 1, Serving Engs = 2, MLEs = 1.
- If GPUs 13-24: SREs = 2, Serving Engs = 3, MLEs = 2.
- If GPUs 25-40: SREs = 3, Serving Engs = 4-5, MLEs = 3.
- Hiring triggers: +1 SRE per +12 GPUs; +1 Serving Eng per +8 GPUs; +1 MLE per +8 model-variants or +10 GPUs (whichever hits first).

COST ASSUMPTIONS (monthly per role):
- SRE fully-burdened: $23,000
- Serving Engineer fully-burdened: $20,000
- MLE fully-burdened: $22,000
- AE fully-burdened: $18,000
- GPU node fully-burdened infra cost: $2,800
- Fixed platform cost bucket (monitoring, infra control plane amortized): $140,000 / month

SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (price elasticity grid):
- Vary price per 1k: [0.0020, 0.0025, 0.0030, 0.0035, 0.0040]
- Demand response model (assumed): volume_change_pct = -8% * (price_change_pct) (i.e., 8% elasticity).
- Example baseline: price=0.0030, daily_tokens=900M tokens/day? (typo illustrative: baseline 900M across customers -> corrected to 900M/day)
Table sample (monthly impact, simplified):
Price | Monthly rev ($k) | Delta rev vs base | GPUs | Margin %
0.0020 | 2,160           | -1,080            | 12   | 52%
0.0025 | 2,700           | -540              | 15   | 55%
0.0030 | 3,240           | 0                 | 18   | 58%
0.0035 | 3,570           | +330              | 20   | 60%
0.0040 | 3,960           | +720              | 22   | 62%
Interpretation: Small increases in price improve margin and reduce needed GPUs slightly (because demand drops); the marginal revenue per additional 0.0005 is ~330k monthly in this simplified model.

PRICE BUCKETS & OPERATIONAL TRIGGERS (prototype rulebook):
- Bucket A (Intro / PLG): $0.0035 /1k, soft cap usage up to 25M tokens/day per customer, auto-quotas applied.
- Bucket B (Volume): $0.0027 /1k, negotiated 6-12 month commits, burst allowed to secondary capacity.
- Bucket C (Reserved Enterprise): $0.0020 /1k base with reserved GPU commits and predictable throughput, requires 6+ GPUs reserved (or equivalent commit) and 24/7 on-call SLA.
Trigger rules (automated):
- If total cluster utilization > 75% sustained for 7 days, open hiring cadence: +1 SRE and +1 Serving Eng approved as "operational scale" hires.
- If average AE quota attainment > 120% for 3 months and net new ARR ramp > $400k/month, hire +1 AE.
- If margin falls below 40% for 2 consecutive months, pause discretionary hiring and fast-track Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization).

RISK NOTES & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: Elasticity underestimation -> revenue drop deeper than model. Mitigation: 30-day price A/B test on 5% of traffic before rollout.
- Risk: Mis-mapped GPU throughput due to new quant kernels. Mitigation: conservative capacity estimate (use 0.8 * measured throughput) and 2-week runway in hiring plan.
- Risk: Sales commit cliffs causing sudden bursts. Mitigation: contract language with phased ramp and burst caps tied to reserved capacity offers.

ACTION ITEMS (next 30 days):
- Finance: run detailed month-by-month P&L variant for three most likely buckets (Assigned: Aria).
- Eng: run capacity bench with quantized 70B and 13B ensembles and report realistic node throughput (Assigned: Daniel).
- Sales: prepare two sample term sheets for Bucket B and C with ramp clauses and proposed discounts (Assigned: Maya).
- Product: implement a lightweight metric in console: cluster_util_7d_avg and price_bucket_delta_30d (Assigned: Evan).

APPENDIX: QUICK CALC EXAMPLE (base):
- Daily tokens = 900M tokens/day; price = $0.003 /1k -> daily revenue = 900,000 * (0.003) = $2,700/day -> monthly ≈ $81,000 (note: earlier row-level sample uses scaled numbers for enterprise mix; this appendix shows per-customer scale math).
- GPUs needed = ceil(900M / 30M) = 30 GPUs -> apply ops/sched adj -> 33 GPUs -> SREs = 3, Serving Engs = 4, MLEs = 3.

DOCUMENT HISTORY:
- 2026-10-12: initial draft, throughput assumptions populated from bench run 2026-09.
- 2026-11-08: updated pricing elasticity to 8% (MLE team reported higher sensitivity).
- 2026-11-15: added explicit hiring triggers and action-item assignments.

NOTES TO REVIEWERS: 
- Please surface any real contract terms that would invalidate the bucket triggers (Sales) and any recent infra pricing changes (Infra Finance).
- This is intentionally conservative in hires; we prefer short hiring bursts with backfill if utilization surprises us.

END OF SHEET
